summary: As of late 2026, the LLM landscape is dominated by a handful of frontier families from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, with strong open-weight competition from DeepSeek, Meta, Mistral, and Qwen. Enterprise adoption increasingly flows through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, which substantially amplify the real-world reach of models available on those platforms. Because the live research data contains several unconfirmed or speculative model names (e.g., GPT-6, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4), this ranking conservatively includes only models whose names are verifiable and currently available.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: The most widely integrated OpenAI model across developer apps and available through Azure OpenAI, giving it enormous enterprise aggregator reach on top of massive direct-API volume.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications requiring multimodal capability and broad tooling support

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: The default workhorse model for Anthropic's coding and agent users, widely adopted and available via AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Azure, maximizing enterprise reach.
models.best_for: Coding assistants and agentic enterprise workflows

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Google's flagship reasoning model with a massive context window, distributed natively through Google Vertex AI and deeply integrated into Google Cloud and Workspace.
models.best_for: Long-context document analysis and reasoning-heavy enterprise tasks

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: The cost-efficient, high-throughput Gemini variant widely used for high-volume production workloads and available through Vertex AI aggregator channels.

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: A 671B-parameter MoE reasoning model (37B active) with open weights and strong HuggingFace download numbers, widely adopted for low-cost math and algorithmic reasoning.
models.best_for: Cost-effective reasoning and open-weight self-hosted deployments

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: A leading open-weight general model delivering near-frontier performance at a fraction of the cost, heavily downloaded on HuggingFace and popular for self-hosting.
models.best_for: Cost-efficient general-purpose tasks and open-weight deployments

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: One of the most downloaded open-weight models on HuggingFace and available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Vertex AI, making it a default enterprise open-model choice.
strengths: Strong general performance for its size
models.best_for: Self-hosted and fine-tuned open-weight enterprise deployments

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's fast, low-cost model used for high-volume and latency-sensitive workloads, benefiting from availability on Bedrock and Vertex AI aggregators.
strengths: Good coding ability for its tier

models.name: o3
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI's dedicated reasoning model adopted for complex math, science, and coding problems, accessible via the OpenAI API and Azure OpenAI.
models.best_for: Complex reasoning, scientific, and advanced coding tasks

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: Alibaba's flagship open-weight MoE model with growing HuggingFace adoption, popular in the open-source community for its strong multilingual and reasoning performance.

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Europe's leading frontier model available through Azure, AWS Bedrock, and Vertex AI, favored by EU enterprises for data-sovereignty and multilingual needs.
models.best_for: European enterprise deployments with data-sovereignty requirements
